nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ be integrable with compact support. Then its Fourier–Laplace transform $z \mapsto \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) \, e^{-2\pi i x z} \, dx$ is complex differentiable at every $z \in \mathbb{C}$, that is, it is entire.
nodes.title: The Fourier–Laplace transform of an integrable compactly supported function is entire

nodes.summary: For every $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real $r$, the Fourier–Laplace transform of $f$ at the complex number $r$, namely $\int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) \, e^{-2\pi i x r} \, dx$, equals the Fourier transform of $f$ at $r$ with the $2\pi$ normalization, $\hat f(r) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{-2\pi i x r} f(x) \, dx$.
nodes.title: Fourier–Laplace transform on the real axis

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the Fourier–Laplace transform of $f$ at $z$ is the Lebesgue integral $\int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) \, e^{-2\pi i x z} \, dx$, taken to be $0$ when the integrand is not integrable.
nodes.title: Fourier–Laplace transform

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ be integrable with compact support, and let $F(z) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) \, e^{-2\pi i x z} \, dx$ be its Fourier–Laplace transform. Then at every $z \in \mathbb{C}$, $F$ is complex differentiable with derivative $F'(z) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) \, (-2\pi i x) \, e^{-2\pi i x z} \, dx$.
nodes.title: Derivative of the Fourier–Laplace transform
